Colorado Springs|United States of Americ.f: Covering 195.761 square miles in 2020, it has the greatest total area of any municipality in Colorado.

Ontario|United States of America.f: Two rival theaters opened across the street from each other, putting 52 screens on one parking lot, more than anywhere else in the US.

Birmingham (AL)|United States of America.f: Four office buildings raised at 20th Street and 1st Avenue North between 1902 and 1912 earned it the name Heaviest Corner on Earth.

Kailua-Kona|United States of America.f: Its all-time low of 56 F is the highest record low in the United States.

Grand Rapids|United States of America.f: It averages 75.6 inches of snow a year, making it one of the snowiest major cities in the United States.

Greensboro|United States of America.f: Four college students began the Woolworth's lunch counter sit-in here on February 1, 1960, and the site is now a civil rights museum.

Long Beach|United States of America.f: Its population grew 690.8 percent in one decade, from 2,252 residents in 1900 to 17,809 in 1910.

San Bernardino|United States of America.f: Richard and Maurice McDonald founded McDonald's and its restaurant concept here in 1940.

Tulsa|United States of America.f: Businessman Cyrus Avery founded the U.S. Highway 66 Association here in 1925, giving Tulsa the nickname Birthplace of Route 66.

Knoxville|United States of America.f: Confederate forces besieged the city for two weeks in 1863, then failed in a fierce 20-minute assault on Fort Sanders.

Fresno|United States of America.f: Bank of America launched BankAmericard here in 1958, choosing a remote city to limit damage if it flopped, and it became Visa.

Sarasota|United States of America.f: John Ringling moved the winter quarters of his circus here in 1927, which later earned the city the name Circus City.

Syracuse|United States of America.f: A townsman named Wilkinson proposed the name in 1820 after Syracuse, Sicily, another place where salt and fresh water mingle.

Albany (NY)|United States of America.f: It is the oldest surviving settlement of the original British Thirteen Colonies north of Virginia.

Rochester (NY)|United States of America.f: By 1838 it was the largest flour-producing city in the United States, which earned it the nickname the Flour City.

Portland (ME)|United States of America.f: A fire on July 4, 1866 destroyed most commercial buildings and half the churches and left over 10,000 people homeless.

Pensacola|United States of America.f: Tristan de Luna landed here with about 1,500 people on 11 ships in 1559, six years before St. Augustine was founded.

Lihue|United States of America.f: Royal Governor Kaikioewa made it his seat of government in 1837, moving it from Waimea, and named it for his own land on Oahu.

Santa Ana|United States of America.f: In 1810 Spanish army sergeant Jose Antonio Yorba was granted land here that he called Rancho Santiago de Santa Ana.

Amarillo|United States of America.f: The US bought the Cliffside gas field in 1927, and the Amarillo helium plant was the world's sole commercial helium producer for many years.

Yuma|United States of America.f: Guinness World Records names it the Sunniest City on Earth, with sunshine at least 91 percent of the year.

Wichita Falls|United States of America.f: In September 2011 it became the first Texas city to have 100 days of 100 F or hotter in a year, beating the 79 days of 1980.

Roswell|United States of America.f: Joe Bauman hit a minor-league record 72 home runs for the 1954 Roswell Rockets.

Dover|United States of America.f: Delaware's capital moved here from New Castle in 1777 for its central location and safety from British raiders on the Delaware River.

Lincoln|United States of America.f: An Omaha senator tried to block the capital move by naming the new city for the assassinated Abraham Lincoln, and it failed.

Huntsville|United States of America.f: It grew 340.3 percent in the 1950s, from 16,437 to 72,365 residents, as Redstone Arsenal's rocket work took off.

Salina|United States of America.f: Temperatures here have ranged from 118 F on August 13, 1936 to minus 31 F on February 13, 1905.

Fort Walton Beach|United States of Ameri.f: Its biggest snowfall on record was 7.5 inches on January 21, 2025, during a rare Gulf Coast blizzard.

Fort Wayne|United States of America.f: The US Army built Fort Wayne in 1794 under General Anthony Wayne, the last of several forts near the Miami town of Kekionga.

Plattsburgh|United States of America.f: During the Cold War, 12 Atlas F missiles sat in silos around the city, ten in New York and two across Lake Champlain in Vermont.

Lubbock|United States of America.f: Its 274-foot Metro Tower is believed to be the tallest building ever to survive a direct hit from an F5 tornado, in 1970.

Bangor|United States of America.f: By 1860 it was the world's largest lumber port, with 150 sawmills and 3,300 lumber ships docking in that year alone.

Portsmouth|United States of America.f: The 1905 treaty ending the Russo-Japanese War was signed at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, earning Theodore Roosevelt a Nobel Peace Prize.

Greenville (SC)|United States of America.f: By 1915 it was known as the Textile Center of the South, with up to 19 cotton mills at its peak.

Dayton|United States of America.f: In 1890 it had been granted more patents per capita than any other US city, and it is where the Wright Flyer was built.

Bakersfield|United States of America.f: Kern County, where the city sits, was the most oil productive county in the United States in 2013.

Toledo|United States of America.f: Ohio and Michigan fought the nearly bloodless Toledo War over a strip five to eight miles wide, and Michigan got more Upper Peninsula.

Duluth|United States of America.f: Its port is the world's farthest inland port accessible to oceangoing ships, about 2,300 miles from the Atlantic.

Billings|United States of America.f: Named for Northern Pacific Railroad president Frederick Billings, it earned the nickname Magic City for its rapid early growth.

Great Falls|United States of America.f: Lewis and Clark's party spent 31 days in the area on a grueling portage around the 10 miles of waterfalls.
